evidence.observation: Bootstrap pass for a fresh project. The method forces setProjectTrusted(false), reloads the settings manager so that state takes effect, and then loads the extension set with includeInlineFactories: true. Because project trust is off, package resolution never collects the project's .pi/extensions entries, so a freshly created project extension is unavailable at this point; only user/global and temporary CLI extensions are returned.

Two-phase trust gate. When resolveProjectTrust is supplied, reload first calls loadProjectTrustExtensions() to build the pre-trust (bootstrap) extension set, then awaits options.resolveProjectTrust({ extensionsResult: preTrustExtensions }) to obtain the explicit decision, and finally applies it via settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted) before reloading settings. The project extension therefore stays out until the caller returns an explicit trusted decision.

Post-trust assembly. The pre-trust extensions are indexed by resolvedPath and their paths (and any pre-existing errors) are excluded from remainingPaths; the remaining paths — which now include the project extension once trust is true — are loaded against the same runtime and merged into an ordered final set. This is the step where the project extension becomes available, reusing rather than re-loading the user/global extensions observed during bootstrap.

Source of the gating observed above: auto-discovered project resources from projectDirs.extensions (cwd/.pi/extensions), prompts and themes are only added when settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() is true, whereas user resources under the agent dir are added unconditionally. With trust forced off during bootstrap, the fresh project extension is never collected.

claims.claim: A freshly created project extension under .pi/extensions is unavailable during the bootstrap pass because loadProjectTrustExtensions() forces project trust off before resolving resources.

reload() exposes only the pre-trust (user/global + temporary) extension set to the trust decision, then applies the explicit boolean via setProjectTrusted before the full resource set is resolved; without a trusted decision the project extension is never loaded.

loadFinalExtensionSet() makes the project extension available only after the trusted decision by reusing the pre-trust extensions and loading the remaining (now project-inclusive) paths into one ordered result.

Project auto-discovery in the package manager collects .pi/extensions only when the settings manager reports the project as trusted, which is the concrete mechanism that keeps the fresh project extension out during bootstrap.

conclusion: The demo confirms the two-phase trust contract for a fresh extension fixture. In phase one, DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() forces project trust off, so package resolution excludes .pi/extensions and the bootstrap extension set contains only user/global extensions; the fresh project extension is unavailable. An explicit trusted decision returned to reload() is applied via setProjectTrusted, after which loadFinalExtensionSet() loads the remaining paths and the project extension becomes available (ordered before the reused user extension). Returning an explicit untrusted decision leaves the project extension absent. This is the behavior asserted by the executable vitest demo and reproduced as a normalized operation result by the dependency-free contract harness.
